title: Hedonic price modelling – How to estimate 𝛽s?
text: Hedonic price modelling – How to estimate 𝛽s? • The main technical challenges facing HMP (typical when dealing complex goods): • Omitted variable biases – when important variables are missing from the regression model • Consequences: biased/incorrect coefficient estimates • Remedies: robustness checks, no direct solutions (no data!) • Misspecification errors – when variables are included in wrong forms • Consequences: biased/incorrect coefficient estimates • Remedies: variable transformations, more flexible estimation methods, … • Multicollinearity – when included variables are highly correlated • Consequences: inflated variances, biased/incorrect coefficient estimates and test results • Remedies: removing correlated variables, orthogonalization, …

title: Why Price (Y) was logged in both models?
text: Why Price (Y) was logged in both models? Logging Data – interpretation of the beta coefficients • When Y is logged, the Y changes by 100*(beta coefficient) percent for a one unit increase in X When X increases by 1 unit, Y increases by 0.55%. • When X is logged, a one percent change in X changes the dependent variable by (beta/100) units When X increase by 1%, Y increases by 0.0115 units or 1.15%. • When both X and Y are logged, beta is the percent change in Y, while X increases by one percent. This relationship is commonly referred in econometrics as elasticity. title: Dummy variables in HPM
text: Dummy variables in HPM • Linear regression models require numerical input, so categorical variables (such as gender, property type, region) need to be converted into a numerical form. • Dummy variables (also known as indicator variables or binary variables) take on values of 0 or 1 to indicate the absence (0) or presence (1) of a particular categorical effect. • Dummy variables are used in regression analysis to convert a categorical variable into a group of dummy variables, which are collectively exhaustive (nothing left out) and mutually exclusive (no overlapping). • For a variable with p categories, only p-1 dummy variables are needed in regression. The omitted category is the reference category. • Each coefficient (𝛽) of a dummy variable represents the difference in the dependent variable (e.g., rent, price) between the reference category and the respective category of the dummy variable.

title: Exercises – rental vs sales markets
text: Exercises – rental vs sales markets 1. Open “Lectures 4-5 Exercises Data.xlsx” in a software of your choice. Examine the data. 2. Generate descriptive statistics of all variables. Note the distribution of ‘Floorarea’. What is the maximum value of this variable? Remove observations with a floor area over 200 squared metres. 3. Make natural log transformation of the following variables: Price, Floorarea, Busstation, Railstation and Airport. Save the file to your work directory. 4. Convert Propertytype and Date into dummy variables. 5. Estimate a hedonic price model for the rental and the sales market, respectively. Include intercept dummies for property type and transaction year. Use both the linear and the log-linear functional forms. 6. Estimate a hedonic price model for the rental market only. Include a slope dummy to check if the effect of Floorarea is different between Detached houses and other types of properties.
